turns.content: I'm working out the local-to-world coordinate convention, treating x as forward and y as leftward based on where the target appears in the H0 image, then using the H4 robot pose (position and yaw) to transform its local target observation into world coordinates for comparison.Comparing that transformed H4 target position to the H0 target position gives a displacement that's mostly rightward and slightly backward, so I'm computing the angle of that displacement to figure out which direction bucket it falls into—it's landing ambiguously between "right" and "back-right," so I'm recomputing the trig values more precisely to nail down which one it actually is.

{"bbox": [0.568, 0.224, 0.760, 0.758], "motion": "right"}
Correction to my earlier replies in this conversation: the H4 target box above is the right one, and the earlier box was wrong. With this box, the target center is at x≈0.66, which is in the center third, so the earlier answer "C" should have been "B".
